1  ACQUISITION, REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT, 2013,
 AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 23.03.2021  PASSED IN LAC.NO.472/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE I ADDITIONAL  DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, BELAGAVI, DISMISSING THE  REFERENCE PETITION FILED UNDER SECTION 64 OF RIGHT TO  FAIR COMPENSATION AND TRANSPARENCY IN LAND  ACQUISITION, REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT, 2013.
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738  MFA No. 100195 of 2022  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
This appeal is listed today in the orders list.
Registry has raised objection relating to payment of Court fee.

2. Learned counsel for the appellants submit that the payment of Court fee is not required in the case, as the appellants are seeking remand of the matter to the Reference Court for fresh consideration in accordance with law, as the Reference Petition is dismissed by the Reference Court for non-prosecution during the period where there was Covid-19 pandemic related restrictions.
3. Learned Government Advocate accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.1 and learned counsel Sri. Umesh. C. Ainapur, accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.2.
The issue relating to the court fee is heard and also the appeal is heard on merits.
5. Learned Government Advocate for the appellants submit that;

5.1. The Reference Petition before the Reference Court seeking enhancement of compensation challenging the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition officer is dismissed for non- prosecution, as the claimants could not appear before the Court to lead evidence on account of Covid-19 pandemic related restrictions.

5.2. The petition could not have been dismissed and it is his submission that the Reference Petition cannot be dismissed for non-prosecution and the same has to be decided on merits based on the available materials on record and the Reference Court has dismissed the petition without applying it's mind to the correctness of the award passed by the Special Land NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 Acquisition Officer by analyzing the same with reference to the claim made in the reference petition.

Girimalla Shivgouda Biradar vs The Special Land Acquisiton Officer on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30726537/
2 5.3.

sentences.text: The appellants have filed this appeal with a prayer to remand the matter and are not seeking any specific amount of compensation before this Court and as the appellants are only praying for remand, to enable the appellants to lead evidence in support of there claim before the Reference Court.

6. In reply, Learned Government Advocate also submits that, unless the proper court fee is paid as required under Section 48 of Karnataka Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, 1958, the appeal cannot be entertained and no order can be passed in favour of the appellants.
7.

entities.text: Karnataka Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, 1958
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondents would submit that the Reference Court has dismissed the petition noticing the fact that the claimants were NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 consistently absent before the Court and after going through the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, has confirmed the same.
Thus, it cannot be treated as dismissal for non- prosecution simplicitor which has to be treated as dismissal on merits.
8. This Court has considered the submissions made at the Bar.

9. The court fee payable in respect of an appeal arising from a decision or an award or order relating to compensation under any Act for the acquisition of property for the public purpose is governed by Section 48 of the Karnataka Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 1958' for brevity).

entities.text: Karnataka Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act, 1958
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Section 48 of the Act of 1958 reads as under:
"The fee payable under this Act on a memorandum of appeal against [ a decision or an award or order] relating to compensation under any Act for the time being in force for NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 the acquisition of property for public purposes shall be computed on the difference between the amount awarded and the amount claimed by the [appellant]".
10. Act of 1958, reads as under:
"64. Refund in cases of remand.- (1) Where a plaint or memorandum of appeal which has been rejected by the lower court is ordered to be received, or where a suit is remanded in appeal for a fresh decision by the lower court, the court making the order or remanding the appeal shall, where the whole decree is reversed and the suit is remanded, and may in other cases direct the refund to the appellant of the full amount of fee paid on the memorandum of appeal; and, if the remand is on second appeal, also on the memorandum of appeal in the first appellate court.
(2) Where an appeal is remanded in second appeal for a fresh decision by the lower appellate court, the High Court remanding the appeal may direct the refund to the appellant of the full amount NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 of fee paid on the memorandum of second appeal:

sentences.text:
3 Provided that, no refund shall be ordered if the remand was caused by the fault of the party who would otherwise be entitled to a refund:
Provided further that, if the order of remand does not cover the whole of the subject matter of the suit, the refund shall not extend to more than so much fee as would have been originally payable on that part of the subject-matter in respect whereof the suit has been remanded."
11.
This Court has also considered the case on merits.
As could be noticed from the impugned order passed by the Reference Court, this order is an order of dismissal for non-prosecution.
It is an admitted fact that the claimants/Appellants didn't appear before the Reference Court to lead any evidence.
The respondents have also not led any evidence.
The reference petition is not barred by limitation.
In view of that there is no evidence on behalf of the claimant, the reference petition has to be dismissed and the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer has to be confirmed.

So I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The reference petition filed under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 is dismissed.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer is confirmed.
Draw award accordingly."
12. On perusal of the aforementioned award, it is explicitly clear that Reference Court has not passed a reasoned order to confirm the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

It is simply held that the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer has to confirmed NC:
2023:KHC-D:10738 as there is no evidence led by the claimants seeking enhancement.
In other words, the Reference Court has not applied its mind as to how the compensation as determined by the Special Land Acquisition Officer is just and fair compensation payable to the claimants.

There is no application of mind by the Reference Court to say that the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer is in tune with the requirement of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013' for brevity).

sentences.text: 4 13. Even though the claimants have not appeared before the Reference Court, the right to property being a constitutional right, if not a fundamental right, the Reference Court is required to apply its mind and to satisfy itself as to whether the compensation is awarded as required under the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 Act of 2013.
Unfortunately such an exercise is not carried out and accordingly dismissed the petition.
14. It is also required to be noticed that this order of dismissal is passed on 23.03.2021.
There is no dispute that, during this period there were several restrictions on amount of Covid-19 pandemic.
The petition could not have been dismissed for non- prosecution for want of appearance of the claimants when there were restrictions owing to Covid-19 pandemic.
15. This being the position, the claimants have made out a case for remand of the matter to the Reference Court.
16. It is also required to be noticed that, under Section 64 of the Act of 1958, the appellants are entitled for refund of court fee in the event of remand of the matter.
The reference petition is dismissed for non-prosecution during the Covid-19 pandemic.

This is valid ground available to the appellants to - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 submit that, there is no need to pay the court fee, as eventually, the court fee, if paid by the appellants, has to be refunded to the appellants in view of the mandate of Section 64 of the Act of 1958.
17. This being the position, the office objection relating to nonpayment of court fee is over-ruled in the back drop of peculiar facts and circumstances of this case.
18. For the reasons signed above, the matter is to be remanded to the trial Court by setting aside the impugned judgment and award.

19. Hence the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed.
ii.
The judgment and award dated 23.03.2021 passed by the I Additional District and Sessions - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10738 Judge, Belagavi, in L.A.C. No.472/2017 are set aside.
